3. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable, the suit is barred by limitation and that the defendant took possession of the property in question with a selami of Taka 16,500.00 from one Nirmal Dutta and the defendant also paid Taka 5,000.00 to the plaintiff as selami. The suit premises is not bonafide required by the plaintiff, The defendant spent Taka 15,000.00 for repairing the premises and for construction of a sanitary latrine. The defendant has been paying rent regularly and got receipts and that no notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was ever served on the defendant The plaintiff once refused to accept the rent for the month of December, 1986 and the defendant deposited the said rent with the House Rent Controller vide Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 1987 and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 9. In the instant case the lease agreement was for two years but after expiry of two years, the terms and conditions continue with the change of rent at Taka 1100.00 to be paid within 7th day of the next month, for which the rent was due. The Courts below have found that the defendant has defaulted in making payment for the month of September and October, 1986 as the rent was paid on 11-11-86 and 8-11-86 in violation of the terms of the said agreement making him to be a defaulter. Since the said agreement is continuing, I am of the view that section 18(5) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance, as has been relied on by the learned Advocate for the petitioner entitling the defendant to pay the rent within 15 days of the next month for which the rent is due, is not applicable and, as such, there is no error of law in the finding of the Courts below treating the defendant to be a defaulter. The courts below also on consideration of the evidence on record found that the plaintiff has bonafide requirement of the suit premises and the notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was also served on the defendant determining the tenancy with effect from November, 1987 and awarded compensation. The said findings are based on appreciation of evidence on record and I have no reason to differ with the said findings as there is no error of law occasioning failure of justice in the impugned judgment.
